title.value: Biomedical image analysis competitions: The state of current participation practice
title.justification: The paper centers on the current practice of participation in biomedical image analysis competitions, as indicated by the title.
title.quote: Biomedical image analysis competitions: The state of current participation practice

extractions.description: The paper discusses the status quo in algorithm development for biomedical image analysis, focusing on practices and bottlenecks faced by participants in IEEE ISBI 2021 and MICCAI 2021 challenges. It provides insights gained from a survey of participants across 80 competitions, covering their expertise, strategies, and characteristics of the algorithms used.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on the practice and challenges of participation in biomedical image analysis competitions, not directly linked to climate or ecological sustainable development themes.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: To shed light on the status quo of algorithm development in the specific field of biomedical imaging analysis, we designed an international survey that was issued to all participants of challenges conducted in conjunction with the IEEE ISBI 2021 and MICCAI 2021 conferences.

primary_category.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on biomedical image analysis, which does not fall under any specific category related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
primary_category.quote: The survey covered participants’ expertise and working environments, their chosen strategies, as well as algorithm characteristics.

secondary_categories.justification: As the paper specifically focuses on biomedical image analysis competitions and not on any secondary themes related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development, it does not align with the secondary categories defined for this task.
secondary_categories.quote: Overall, 94% of all solutions were deep learning-based. Of these, 84% were based on standard architectures.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not focus on sub-categories associated with Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development but rather on biomedical image analysis practices.
primary_sub_category.quote: A majority (86%) of the challenge participants who responded were affiliated with academic institutions.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper's focus on biomedical image analysis and participation strategies does not overlap with any specific sub-category of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Almost all respondents had an academic degree. In terms of the highest degree, 45% had a master’s degree, 27% had a doctoral degree, and 24% had a bachelor’s degree.

applications.justification: The applications discussed in the paper pertain to biomedical image analysis and competition practices, not applications related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
applications.quote: Validation of biomedical image analysis algorithms is typically conducted through so-called challenges - large international benchmarking competitions that compare algorithm performance on identical datasets.

new_primary_category.justification: There is no indication from the paper that it should be assigned a new category related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
new_primary_category.quote: The number of international benchmarking competitions is steadily increasing in various fields of machine learning (ML) research and practice.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not necessitate the creation of a new sub-category related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: A notable gap in the literature regarding insights into current common practice in challenges was identified and addressed in the survey results.
